links.comparator_used: Initial model version (0.14.0/first calibrated version) before developer updates, within a before-after lifecycle design; there was no separate static-model arm
links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy (AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity), technical defect rate and clinical assessment score across successive updated versions
links.effect: AUC 0.73 to 0.91 (+24.7%), accuracy 0.77 to 0.89, sensitivity 0.62 to 0.85, specificity 0.84 to 0.93; technical defects 9.0% to 1.0%; clinical assessment score 63.4 to 72.0
links.tradeoff: Architectural updates required repeat calibration testing. Technical defects still spiked in months 12 and 19. The clinical score dipped in months 15-16 when the expert reviewer changed. The calibration set had only 100 studies and there was no non-updated control arm.
links.quote: Specifically, the AUC rose by 24.7% (from 0.73 to 0.91), the accuracy improved by 15.6% (from 0.77 to 0.89), sensitivity grew by 37.1% (from 0.62 to 0.85), and specificity increased by 10.7% (from 0.84 to 0.93).

design_hint: lifecycle testing with continuous monitoring and feedback-driven updates
